title: A 21st Century Parable
author: Paul Kirschner
summary: Kirschner relates a cautionary tale about a teacher who violates a clear classroom smartphone policy by allowing students to use phones for an assignment. When supervision breaks down and images spread on social media, the teacher responds with punishment rather than reflection. Kirschner argues that credible education requires teachers to model and uphold the rules they establish. The essay critiques approaches focused on rule-breaking without addressing the teacher's role in creating the situation. He emphasizes that education depends on consistent role modeling where adults demonstrate that rules apply equally to everyone.
points: Teachers must model the behaviors they expect: Credible education depends on adults following the same rules they enforce. Asking only students to reflect without teacher accountability undermines trust.
Rule violations require reflection from leaders too: When teachers break policy, an apology and personal accountability are essential, not just punishment of students.
Inconsistent enforcement undermines authority: If rules apply only to students and not to teachers, students learn that authority is arbitrary rather than principled.
Professional modeling shapes culture more than lectures: Students learn from what adults do, not from what they say students should do.
Education requires integrity alignment: Rules matter less than consistent adherence to them by those in positions of authority.
quotes: Education is not only about rules, but about role modeling. Anyone who wants to educate credibly must show that the rules apply to themselves as well.
The rules were broken by the teacher; professional judgment was lacking; and the situation arose primarily because of that.
In such cases, reflection should not be demanded only from pupils, but also from the teacher.
An apology to the pupils and their parents would be appropriate, and perhaps the teacher should write an essay on the importance of adhering to agreed-upon rules.
The question is not only 'How do pupils behave?' but also 'What behavior do teachers model as professionals?” Archived from Paul Kirschner on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
